question: For a read-heavy product catalog API, should we cache at the HTTP layer (CDN / reverse proxy) or in the application layer (in-process or shared cache)? Assume 50k req/s, 95% reads, catalog updated a few times an hour.
background: The catalog is mostly static within an hour but a price or availability change must be visible within about a minute. Responses are JSON, 2-20 KB. The service runs behind a CDN already used for static assets. There is a shared cache cluster available. Team is small and wants low operational load.
constraints: Stale price shown to a user for more than ~60s is a correctness problem, not just a UX one.
The team does not want to run a new stateful service if an existing layer can do the job.
Cost of the CDN is per-request plus egress; the shared cache cluster is already paid for.
